chunks: Sa'd ibn 'Abdillah narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mansur ibn Hazim, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who borrowed money, and the year passed while it was in his possession, he said: 'If the one who lent it to him pays its zakat, then there is no zakat upon him; and if he does not pay, the borrower pays.'
ai.seo_question: Who is responsible for paying zakat on money borrowed from someone else?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the mechanism of zakat on debt (al-qard) by linking the borrower's liability to the lender's fulfillment of their own zakat obligation, reflecting the Shia principle of avoiding double taxation on the same wealth. It highlights the practical scholarly distinction between the debt being in the possession of the borrower versus the lender's status, ensuring the financial burden is assigned to the party who effectively holds the value during the haul. This ruling is foundational in fiqh al-zakat for determining who bears the cost when wealth circulates between parties.
